chunks: And ʿAlī عليه السلام ruled regarding four men who looked into the lion's pit,
then one of them fell, so he clung to the second, and the second clung to the third, and the third clung to the fourth, until some of them caused the others to fall onto the lion.

So he ruled concerning the first that he was the lion’s prey, and he imposed upon his family one-third of the diyyah for the family of the second. And he imposed upon the family of the second, for the family of the third, two-thirds of the diyyah. And he imposed upon the family of the third, for the family of the fourth, the full diyyah.

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: blood money paid as legal compensation for a killing
key_terms.ثُلُثَ الدِّيَةِ: one-third of the legal blood compensation
key_terms.ثُلُثَيِ الدِّيَةِ: two-thirds of the legal blood compensation
key_terms.زُبْيَةِ الْأَسَدِ: a pit or trap prepared for a lion
key_terms.فَرِيسَةُ الْأَسَدِ: the prey of the lion; one directly killed by it

ai.seo_question: How did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام rule on blood money when several people fell one after another into a lion’s pit?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling by Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام concerning layered liability in an accidental chain of deaths. It assigns differing portions of the diyyah according to each person’s causal involvement, while treating the first as directly killed by the lion.
